History

Since before the time of Aristotle\, the stars and planets have been thought to be governed by geometric laws

Aristotle and Ptolemy both suggested that Earth was at the center of the universe and that all objects moved around it in uniform circular motion

The circle was a mystical and perfect structure to the ancients\, and they projected these ideas onto the heavens

It was thought that invisible crystalline spheres carried the planets and all other objects in space around the Earth in perfect circular motion

The ancients believed that there were four fundamental elements on Earth: air\, water\, fire and Earth\, and that a fifth\, the Quintessence or “ether” was perfect and incorruptible and held all things together

Aristotle’s solar system was __ __teleological \, emphasizing perfect order and purpose in the natural world

This is a Greek word meaning the opposite of chaos ;

The order or harmony of nature

Importantly\, it was not based on empirical observation\, but philosophical premises emphasizing __ _cosmos _ __in the universe

Newton

Besides developing the the Laws of Motion on Earth\, Isaac Newton examined the motion of the planets and Luna

Since falling objects accelerate\, they must have a force exerted on them

Whenever a force is exerted __ _on _ __an object\, it was exerted __ _by _ __some other object

According to legend\, Newton observed an apple falling from the top of a tree and was apparently struck with a moment of realization

If gravity works at the tops of trees\, or even the tops of mountains\, perhaps it acts all the way to the Moon

He did not have a satisfactory way of explaining how Earth could attract objects without touching them\, and many scientists initially rejected his “ spooky action at a distance ”

A New Center

Copernicus\, Galileo\, Kepler\, and others had been measuring the positions of astronomical objects\, particularly the moon

It was discovered that the Moon kept an almost perfectly circular orbit around the Earth

Newton set about calculating the force of attraction that would keep Luna in uniform circular motion

An Inverse Square Law

Newton discovered the gravity seems to obey an inverse square law: that is\, its magnitude decreases proportionally to the square of the distance between two objects:

It turns out that this kind of relationship governs many things in nature

Using the latest observational values for the period of the Moon\, he was able to compute the (average) distance between Luna and Earth

A New Center

This is the acceleration of Earth on Luna\, not gravity when you stand on Luna

__Luna is approximately 60 Earth radii away\, so it feels a gravitational force of __

__ or the force of gravity here on Earth’s surface (0.00272 m/s__ 2 )

According to his own third law of motion\, the moon must also exert an equal and opposite force on the Earth

The symmetry of the Newton’s third law

Thus\, the symmetry of those forces must be proportional to both masses\, leading to:

The gravitational force between to objects is:

directly proportional to the product of the masses and

inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them

\[\vec{F_g} \propto \frac{m_{Earth} \cdot m_{object}}{r^2}\]

Newton’s math failed to explain the motion of the planets around the Earth\, but worked beautifully to explain Kepler and Brahe’s measurements in a heliocentric model

A magnum opus

Newton’s pivotal mathematical description is now called the __ __Law of Universal Gravitation \, and is written as:

__Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. __

__This force always acts along a line joining the two particles. __

You are here

Forever falling, forever missing the ground

Satellites are put into orbit by accelerating them to sufficiently high tangential speeds

If the speed is too low\, the Earth’s gravity will de-orbit the satellite

__If the speed is too high\, Earth’s gravity will be insufficient to hold it and it will escape __

Satellites, Orbit, and “Weightlessness”

There and back again

“Weightlessness” in orbit

People and objects orbiting Earth are said to experience __ _apparent _ __weightlessness .

This feels true to the person\, but it is only true __ __from their own frame of reference

When the elevator is at rest\, the normal force balances out the weight of the person

When the elevator falls\, the person and elevator accelerate downward at equal rates

At rest:

While falling:

But the acceleration of all objects (elevator\, bag\, person) is the same so relative to one another they do not __ _appear _ __to accelerate

Mind what planet (parent) body you are working with

Gravity is still acting on all objects and is still equal to ma g

At sufficient distances from Earth (or another source of gravity)\, astronauts and spacecraft could experience “ true __ __ weightlessness ”\, the absence of a (significant) gravitational force in any direction
